questions.question:
A string is wrapped around the rim of a wheel of moment of inertia 0.40kgm2 and radius 10 cm. The wheel is free to rotate about its axis. Initially the wheel is at rest. The string is now pulled by a force of 40 N. The angular velocity of the wheel after 10 s is xrad/s, where \(x\) is ____

[JEE Main 2024, 9 Apr (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
The force is applied tangentially to the rim of the wheel.

τ=F×r\tau = F \times r

Given F=40 N and r=10 cm=0.1 m:

τ=40×0.1=4 Nm\tau = 40 \times 0.1 = 4 \text{ Nm}

Find the Angular Acceleration (α)

Using the rotational analog of Newton's Second Law (τ=Iα):

α=τI\alpha = \frac{\tau}{I}

Given I=0.40 kgm2:

α=40.40=10 rad/s2\alpha = \frac{4}{0.40} = 10 \text{ rad/s}^2

Determine the Angular Velocity (ω)

Using the first equation of rotational motion (ω=ω0+αt):

Since the wheel starts from rest, ω0=0. Given t=10 s:

ω=0+(10×10)\omega = 0 + (10 \times 10)
ω=100 rad/s\omega = 100 \text{ rad/s}

The value of x is 100.

questions.question:
Let \(|\cos \theta \cos (60-\theta) \cos (60+\theta)| \leq \frac{1}{8}, \theta \in[0,2 \pi]\). Then, the sum of all \(\theta \in[0,2 \pi]\), where \(\cos 3 \theta\) attains its maximum value, is

 

[JEE Main 2024, 9 Apr (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
We know that

cosθcos60°-θcos60°+θ=14cos3θ

\(|\cos \theta \cos (60-\theta) \cos (60+\theta)| \leq \frac{1}{8}\)

⇒14cos3θ≤18

\( \Rightarrow|\cos 3 \theta| \leq \frac{1}{2} \)
\( \Rightarrow-\frac{1}{2} \leq \cos 3 \theta \leq \frac{1}{2}\)

⇒ maximum value of \(\cos 3 \theta=\frac{1}{2}\), here

\( \Rightarrow 3 \theta=2 \mathrm{n} \pi \pm \frac{\pi}{3} \)
\( \theta=\frac{2 \mathrm{n} \pi}{3} \pm \frac{\pi}{9}\)

As \(\theta \in[0,2 \pi]\) possible values are

\(\theta=\left\{\frac{\pi}{9}, \frac{5 \pi}{9}, \frac{7 \pi}{9}, \frac{11 \pi}{9}, \frac{13 \pi}{9}, \frac{17 \pi}{9}\right\}\)
Whose sum is \(\frac{\pi}{9}+\frac{5 \pi}{9}+\frac{7 \pi}{9}+\frac{11 \pi}{9}+\frac{13 \pi}{9}+\frac{17 \pi}{9}=\frac{54 \pi}{9}=6 \pi\)

questions.question:
A ray of light coming from the point \(P (1,2)\) gets reflected from the point Q on the \(x-\)axis and then passes through the point \(R(4,3).\) If the point \(S(h, k)\) is such that \(PQRS\) is a parallelogram, then hk2 is equal to:

 

[JEE Main 2024, 9 Apr (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
Reflect the point \(P(1,2)\) in the \(x\)-axis to obtain \(P'(1,-2)\).

By the law of reflection, the path \(P\to Q\to R\) becomes the straight line \(P'QR\).

Therefore, \(Q\) is the intersection of the line \(P'R\) with the \(x\)-axis.

The slope of the line through \(P'(1,-2)\) and \(R(4,3)\) is \(\dfrac{3-(-2)}{4-1}=\dfrac{5}{3}\).

Hence its equation is \(y+2=\dfrac{5}{3}(x-1)\).

At the \(x\)-axis, \(y=0\).

Therefore, \(2=\dfrac{5}{3}(x-1)\).

Hence \(6=5x-5\), so \(x=\dfrac{11}{5}\).

Thus \(Q\left(\dfrac{11}{5},0\right)\).

For parallelogram \(PQRS\), the diagonals bisect each other, so \(P+R=Q+S\).

Therefore, \(S=P+R-Q\).

Hence \(S=\left(1+4-\dfrac{11}{5},2+3-0\right)=\left(\dfrac{14}{5},5\right)\).

Thus \(h=\dfrac{14}{5}\) and \(k=5\).

Therefore, \(hk^2=\dfrac{14}{5}\cdot25=70\).

Hence the correct option is \(\mathrm{A}\).

questions.question:
The solution of the differential equation x2+y2dx-5xydy=0,y(1)=0, is : 

 

[JEE Main 2024, 9 Apr (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
The differential equation is

\((x^2+y^2)\,dx-5xy\,dy=0\)

\(\Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{x^2+y^2}{5xy}\)

Put \(v=y^2\).

\(\Rightarrow \dfrac{dv}{dx}=2y\dfrac{dy}{dx}\)

\(\Rightarrow \dfrac{dv}{dx}=\dfrac{2x}{5}+\dfrac{2v}{5x}\)

\(\Rightarrow \dfrac{dv}{dx}-\dfrac{2}{5x}v=\dfrac{2x}{5}\)

The integrating factor is

\(\mathrm{I.F.}=e^{\int-\frac{2}{5x}\,dx}=x^{-2/5}\)

\(\Rightarrow \dfrac{d}{dx}(vx^{-2/5})=\dfrac{2}{5}x^{3/5}\)

Integrating, we get

\(vx^{-2/5}=\dfrac{x^{8/5}}{4}+C\)

\(\Rightarrow v=\dfrac{x^2}{4}+Cx^{2/5}\)

Using \(y(1)=0\), we get

\(\Rightarrow C=-\dfrac{1}{4}\)

\(\Rightarrow y^2=\dfrac{x^2-x^{2/5}}{4}\)

\(\Rightarrow x^2-4y^2=x^{2/5}\)

Raising both sides to the fifth power gives

\(\left|x^2-4y^2\right|^5=x^2\)

The correct option is \(A\).

\(\vec c=\vec a-\vec b=(\alpha-5)\hat i+\hat j-2\hat k\)

\(\dfrac{1}{2}|\vec a\times\vec b|=5\sqrt{6}\)

\(\Rightarrow |\vec a\times\vec b|^2=600\)

\(\Rightarrow \vec c=3\hat i+\hat j-2\hat k\)

questions.question:

where \(a , b \in Z.\) If \(f\) is continuous at x=π2, then a2+b2 is equal to _____.

 

[JEE Main 2024, 9 Apr (Shift 1)]

As \(x\to\dfrac{\pi}{2}^-\), \(8x\to4\pi\),

Therefore,

\(\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\pi/2^-}\left(\dfrac87\right)^{\tan8x}=1\).

Continuity gives \(a-8=1\),

Since \(a,b\) are integers and \(a=9\), this gives \(b=0\).

questions.question:
The sum of the square of the modulus of the elements in the set {z=a+ib:a,b∈Z,z∈C,|z-1|≤1,|z-5|≤|z-5i|} 

is _______.

 

[JEE Main 2024, 9 Apr (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(z=a+ib\), where \(a,b\in\mathbb Z\).

The condition \(|z-1|\leq1\) gives

\((a-1)^2+b^2\leq1\).

Since \(a\) and \(b\) are integers, both \((a-1)^2\) and \(b^2\) are non-negative integers.

The possible cases are:

\((a-1)^2=0\) and \(b^2=0\), giving \((a,b)=(1,0)\);

\((a-1)^2=1\) and \(b^2=0\), giving \((a,b)=(0,0),(2,0)\);

\((a-1)^2=0\) and \(b^2=1\), giving \((a,b)=(1,1),(1,-1)\).

Thus, the possible points are

\((1,0),(0,0),(2,0),(1,1),(1,-1)\).

The second condition is \(|z-5|\leq|z-5i|\).

Squaring both sides,

\((a-5)^2+b^2\leq a^2+(b-5)^2\).

\(a^2-10a+25+b^2\leq a^2+b^2-10b+25\).

Therefore, \(-10a\leq-10b\),

so \(b\leq a\).

Each of the five listed points satisfies \(b\leq a\).

Their squared moduli are

\(|1|^2=1\),

\(|0|^2=0\),

\(|2|^2=4\),

\(|1+i|^2=2\),

and \(|1-i|^2=2\).

Therefore, the required sum is

\(1+0+4+2+2=9\).

questions.question:
Let the set of all positive values of λ, for which the point of local minimum of the function 1+xλ2-x2 satisfies x2+x+2x2+5x+6<0, be (α,β). Then α2+β2 is equal to _______.

 

[JEE Main 2024, 9 Apr (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(g(x)=1+x(\lambda^2-x^2)=1+\lambda^2x-x^3\), where \(\lambda>0\).

Then \(g'(x)=\lambda^2-3x^2\)

The stationary points satisfy

\(\lambda^2-3x^2=0\),

so \(x=\pm\dfrac{\lambda}{\sqrt{3}}\)

Also, \(g''(x)=-6x\)

At \(x=-\dfrac{\lambda}{\sqrt{3}}\), we have

\(g''(x)=2\sqrt{3}\lambda>0\)

so this point is the point of local minimum

Let its abscissa be \(u=-\dfrac{\lambda}{\sqrt{3}}\)

The numerator of the given fraction is always positive

because \(u^2+u+2=\left(u+\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2+\dfrac{7}{4}>0\)

Therefore, \(\dfrac{u^2+u+2}{u^2+5u+6}<0\) is possible only when \((u+2)(u+3)<0\)

Hence, \(-3<u<-2\)

Using \(u=-\dfrac{\lambda}{\sqrt{3}}\)

we get \(-3<-\dfrac{\lambda}{\sqrt{3}}<-2\)

Therefore, \(2\sqrt{3}<\lambda<3\sqrt{3}\)

Thus, the interval endpoints are

\(\alpha=2\sqrt{3}\) and \(\beta=3\sqrt{3}\)

Hence, \(\alpha^2+\beta^2=(2\sqrt{3})^2+(3\sqrt{3})^2=12+27=39\)

questions.question:
The remainder when 4282024 is divided by \(21\) is

 

[JEE Main 2024, 9 Apr (Shift 1)]

Let limn→∞nn4+1-2nn2+1n4+1+nn4+16-8nn2+4n4+16+…+nn4+n4-2n·n2n2+n2n4+n4 be πk, using only the principal values of the inverse trigonometric functions. Then k2 is equal to ______.

 

[JEE Main 2024, 9 Apr (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
Let the given sum be \(S_n\).

Its \(r\)-th term is \(\dfrac{n}{\sqrt{n^4+r^4}}-\dfrac{2nr^2}{(n^2+r^2)\sqrt{n^4+r^4}}\).

Taking the common denominator \((n^2+r^2)\sqrt{n^4+r^4}\),

the numerator becomes \(n(n^2+r^2)-2nr^2=n(n^2-r^2)\).

Therefore, \(S_n=\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{n}\dfrac{n(n^2-r^2)}{(n^2+r^2)\sqrt{n^4+r^4}}\).

Dividing the numerator and denominator of each term by \(n^4\), we get

\(S_n=\dfrac{1}{n}\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{n}\dfrac{1-(r/n)^2}{(1+(r/n)^2)\sqrt{1+(r/n)^4}}\).

Hence \(\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}S_n=\displaystyle\int_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1-x^2}{(1+x^2)\sqrt{1+x^4}}\,dx\).

Put \(u=\dfrac{\sqrt2\,x}{\sqrt{1+x^4}}\).

Then \(u=\sqrt2\,x(1+x^4)^{-1/2}\).

Therefore, \(\dfrac{du}{dx}=\sqrt2(1+x^4)^{-1/2}-2\sqrt2\,x^4(1+x^4)^{-3/2}=\dfrac{\sqrt2(1-x^4)}{(1+x^4)^{3/2}}\).

Also, \(1+u^2=1+\dfrac{2x^2}{1+x^4}=\dfrac{(1+x^2)^2}{1+x^4}\).

Thus, \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\tan^{-1}u=\dfrac{u'}{1+u^2}=\dfrac{\sqrt2(1-x^2)}{(1+x^2)\sqrt{1+x^4}}\).

Therefore, \(\displaystyle\int_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1-x^2}{(1+x^2)\sqrt{1+x^4}}\,dx=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\left[\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt2\,x}{\sqrt{1+x^4}}\right)\right]_{0}^{1}\).

At \(x=1\), the argument is \(1\), and at \(x=0\), the argument is \(0\).

Hence the limit is \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}-0\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{4\sqrt2}\).

Since the limit is written as \(\dfrac{\pi}{k}\), we get \(k=4\sqrt2\).

Therefore, \(k^2=32\).

questions.question:
Let the centre of a circle, passing through the points \((0,0),(1,0)\) and touching the circle x2+y2=9, be \((h, k).\) Then for all possible values of the coordinates of the centre \((h, k),\) 4h2+k2 is equal to _______ .

 

[JEE Main 2024, 9 Apr (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
Let the required circle have centre \((h,k)\) and radius \(R\).

Since it passes through \((0,0)\),

\(R^2=h^2+k^2\).

Since it also passes through \((1,0)\),

\((1-h)^2+k^2=R^2\).

\((1-h)^2+k^2=h^2+k^2\)

\(\Rightarrow 1-2h+h^2=h^2\)

\(\Rightarrow h=\dfrac{1}{2}\)

The distance between the centre \((h,k)\) and the origin is \(\sqrt{h^2+k^2}=R\).

The fixed circle \(x^2+y^2=9\) has centre at the origin and radius \(3\).

External touching would require \(R=R+3\), which is impossible.

For internal touching,

\(R=3-R\).

\(\Rightarrow 2R=3\)

\(\Rightarrow R=\dfrac{3}{2}\)

\(\Rightarrow h^2+k^2=R^2=\dfrac{9}{4}\)

\(\Rightarrow 4(h^2+k^2)=9\)
